Passive of Modal Verbs: Could and Should

When we want to give importance to the object of a sentence or when the subject is not important or unknown, the passive voice is used. The noun or noun phrase that is the object of an active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
This is the passive voice structure:
Cloud computing could be implemented to distribute technology as a service on demand over the internet.
This way, customers could be benefited and companies can decrease the costs of IT services.
Hidden charges should be avoided as well.
The agreed positions should be reflected in the IP clause in the contract, if this were the case.
Subject + Modal Verb + Be + Past participle + Complement
The passive voice is used with the modal verb could to talk about present or future possibility.

Inseparable phrasal verbs cannot introduce the object of the sentence between the verb and the preposition or adverb.

When you use inseparable phrasal verbs, you must always place the object pronoun after the preposition. It is not grammatically correct to separate the phrasal verb to introduce the object of the sentence between its elements.
For instance, get away with means to manage to do something wrong without getting negative consequences. If we separate this phrasal verb, the sentence doesn't make sense:
Suppliers broke the law and got away with it. (Correct)
Suppliers broke the law and got it away with. (Incorrect)
The phrasal verb look into, which means to investigate, is another example of an inseparable phrasal verb:
Providers can get away with charging hidden fees.
Besides, you've got to look into the Intellectual Property Rights or IPR.
Companies must look into contractual protection benefits. (Correct)
Companies must look contractual protection benefits into. (Incorrect)

images.text: Daniel: We should go over the cloud contracts today.

Sasha: As you already know, cloud computing could be implemented to distribute technology as a service on demand over the internet. This way, customers could be benefited from economies, and companies can decrease the costs of IT services.
Daniel: What are some rules to consider when negotiating cloud contracts?
Sasha: First, liability should be considered carefully.
Daniel: Because it's usual for suppliers to reject liability in case of data loss?
Sasha: Exactly! Besides, you got to look into the Intellectual Property Rights or IPR. The agreed positions should be reflected in the IP clause in the contract if this were the case.
Daniel: Hidden charges should be avoided as well. Right?
Sasha: Of course. Providers can get away with charging hidden fees. A termination of the contract could also be imposed.
Daniel: I guess we must be aware of the possibility of finishing the contract sooner than expected.
Sasha: Correct. Moreover, the governing law and jurisdiction should be checked in case an issue arises in the future.
Daniel: That's very convenient in case a party backs out of the deal.
Sasha: Finally, a grace period should be provided after the contract is expired to recover data and to delete it after the deal is terminated.
Daniel: That rule is called the lock-in and exit. What about the suitable contractual protections?

Sasha: When you choose a cloud supplier, you must look into the contractual and pricing documents in advance. You need to take into consideration if the suggested contract presents suitable protection measures in the case of data loss, as well.
Daniel: It's basically about ensuring the cloud contract is following every rule we have discussed.
Sasha: Yes! And, if you get the feeling something is not working, do not sign the agreement.
